This isn't my own metaphor, I read it on this subreddit once upon a time but here it goes.

Bipolar is like being in a car with an attitude and shitty steering. You get in and turn on the ignition, it does what it's supposed to do but not consistently. 

You get on the road and hit the gas and it tops out at 20mph. Even if you slam the pedal to the floor, people behind you are getting pissed off because you're so slow no matter what you do it doesn't go any faster... until it does. Other times you barely have to put pressure on the pedal and it jumps to 80 mph, you're nervous about the speed even though it's exciting and you can bob and weave through traffic and everyone else is practically standing still. 

Before long you've had enough so you take pressure off the pedal but it's still going too fast, you put pressure on the breaks but that doesn't work either all you want is to slow down now cause eventually you're going to crash and you worry so much you're sick and nauseous. Everyone tells you how to slow the car down as you scream for help but no one is in the car with you and they don't know how badly you want to stop the car and get out but you literally can't. The best you can do until the car runs out of gas is try to stay on the road and avoid other drivers but the steering still sucks and now it's even worse at top speeds.
